extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants (utility applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the required parts, form, content, arrangement, and formalities of a U.S. utility patent application specification (including abstracts, drawings, sequence listings, and language/format requirements) for filing and examination at the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of illegible portions of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: In bracket 1, identify the part of the specification that is illegible: all of the specification; or certain pages of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified bracket to indicate whether the entire specification or particular pages are illegible. Do not use the form paragraph for reissue applications or reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unauthorized alterations and interlineations
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(c) relating to interlineations and other alterations is strictly enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should enforce no unauthorized interlineations/alterations (see In re Swanberg and MPEP § 605.04(a)). Use appropriate objection practice when alterations are detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet size, margin, and quality requirements for application-as-filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Application-as-filed must meet the sheet size/margin and quality requirements of 37 CFR 1.52 and 1.84(f) and (g); if not, certified copies may be illegible or ineffective as priority documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If papers are noncompliant (e.g., legal size, shiny/non-white), USPTO will perform exception processing (reduce size, attempt enhancement) to image-scan into IFW database. Certified copies are made from the application-as-filed records; if originals are illegible, certified copies will be illegible. Applicants filing noncompliant papers will be required to file substitute papers that comply with 37 CFR requirements, but substitute papers filed after the filing date will not be treated as the original disclosure for certified-copy purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file substitute papers for noncompliant filings
rubrics_metrics.description: If application papers are filed that do not meet sheet size/margin and quality requirements, the USPTO will require the applicant to file substitute papers that do comply with 37 CFR 1.52 and 1.84(e), (f) and (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute papers provide an image- and OCR-scannable copy for printing/publishing. However, papers submitted after the filing date will not be treated as original disclosure for certified copies or other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to use metric (S.I.) units
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent applicants should use the metric (S.I.) units followed by the equivalent English units when describing their inventions in the specifications of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimizes future need to convert dimensions when using printed patents as research and prior art search documents. Explains S.I. origin and recommendation to list S.I. first, then English equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English application filing and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application filed in a language other than English requires an English translation, a statement that the translation is accurate, and the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i); provisional applications filed in a non-English language do not require an English translation at filing but will require one if benefit is claimed later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation/statement/fees are not filed, applicant will be notified and given time to file or risk abandonment. A subsequently filed English translation must contain complete identifying data to permit association. The translation must be literal, accompanied by an accuracy statement, and a signed request that the English translation be used for examination. If idiomatic English/US practice issues exist, include a preliminary amendment to make necessary changes without introducing new matter (35 U.S.C. 132). Failure to timely file will result in abandonment. Applicants are advised this procedure is for emergency situations and should not be routine due to potential errors and administrative burden. Recommended that original filing include a cover letter and self-addressed return postcard containing identifying data in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and graphics limitations in the written description
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical illustrations, diagrammatic views, flow-charts, and diagrams in the descriptive portion of the specification do not come within 37 CFR 1.58(a) (which permits tables, chemical and mathematical formulas in the specification in lieu of formal drawings). The written description portion of the specification must not contain drawings or flow diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should object and request formal drawings under 37 CFR 1.81 when an application contains graphs, drawings, or flow charts in the specification. A claim may incorporate by reference to a specific figure or table where there is no practical way to define the invention in words (see MPEP § 2173.05(s)). The description may contain tables but the same tables must not be included both in the drawings as a figure and in the description (applications under 35 U.S.C. 371 are excluded). Claims may contain tables if necessary to conform to 35 U.S.C. 112 or otherwise desirable; when printed the table will not be part of the claim but will be referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks and browser-executable code prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperlinks and other forms of browser-executable code (especially commercial site URLs) must not be included in a patent application; incorporation by reference by hyperlink or other browser-executable code is not permitted (37 CFR 1.57(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include a URL between “< >” and http:// followed by address. If such embeds are present, examiners should object and require deletion. Exceptions: nucleotide/amino acid sequence data placed between “< >” are not considered hyperlinks (see 37 CFR 1.821–1.825). Do not object where the hyperlinks/browser-executable codes themselves (rather than the content of the linked site) are necessary to meet 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, and applicant does not intend them to be active; the Office will disable hyperlinks when preparing text for the web database. The requirement to delete does not apply to electronic documents listed on forms PTO-892 and PTO/SB/08 where the electronic document is identified by reference to a URL. Attempts to incorporate subject matter by hyperlink should be treated as improper incorporation by reference (use form paragraphs 6.19/6.19.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection practice for embedded hyperlinks or browser-executable code
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.29.04 Disclosure Objected To, Embedded Hyperlinks or Other Forms of Browser-Executable Code — The disclosure is objected to because it contains an embedded hyperlink and/or other form of browser-executable code. Applicant is required to delete the embedded hyperlink and/or other form of browser-executable code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note lists examples and exceptions, and tells examiners when to use form paragraphs and when not to object (e.g., hyperlinks are part of the invention and not intended to be active). Also points to MPEP § 608.01(p) for incorporation-by-reference issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement/order of application elements
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.77: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Utility application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet; (4) Specification; (5) Drawings; (6) Executed oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification should include the sections in order: Title; Cross-reference to related applications; Statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; Names of parties to joint research agreement; Reference to sequence listing/computer program listing appendix on compact disc; Background; Brief summary; Brief description of views of drawings; Detailed description; Claim(s); Abstract; Sequence listing if on paper. Section headings should be uppercase without underlining or bold. If no text follows a heading, use “Not Applicable.” Provisional applications are recommended to follow same format; ADS can be used to supply some data; if discrepancy between ADS and other parts, ADS controls except for naming and citizenship (see 37 CFR 1.76(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section heading formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the specification sections (Title through Sequence Listing) should be preceded by a section heading in uppercase and without underlining or bold type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no text follows the section heading, state “Not Applicable.” Recommended that provisional applications follow the same general format although claims are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention should be brief but technically accurate, preferably from two to seven words, and may not contain more than 500 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the title at the top of the first page of the specification unless the title is provided in an application data sheet (see 37 CFR 1.72(a) and MPEP § 606).

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the invention content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Background of the Invention should set forth: (1) Field of the Invention — a statement of the field of art; and (2) Description of the Related Art — description of the related art known to the applicant including references to specific related art and problems solved by the invention (including information disclosed under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items may be titled “Technical Field” and “Background Art.” Include problems in prior art which are solved by applicant’s invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief summary of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary or general statement of the invention as set forth in 37 CFR 1.73; separate and distinct from the abstract and directed toward the invention rather than the disclosure as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May point out advantages of the invention or how it solves prior art problems; in chemical cases, point out utility. Nature and gist of the inventive concept should be set forth if possible; objects should be treated briefly and only to the extent they contribute to understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of the drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to and brief description of the drawing(s) as set forth in 37 CFR 1.74.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief descriptions of the several views of the drawings under the appropriate section heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of the invention (preferred embodiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the preferred embodiment(s) of the invention as required in 37 CFR 1.71. The description should be as short and specific as is necessary to describe the invention adequately and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventional elements widely known need not be described in detail unless necessary for understanding; where complicated subject matter or uncommon elements are involved, refer to another patent or readily available publication which adequately describes the subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page (37 CFR 1.52(b)(3)). Where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step of the claim should be separated by a line indentation. There may be plural indentations to further segregate subcombinations or related steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.75 and MPEP 608.01(i)-(p) for additional guidance. Claims should be formatted to clearly separate elements/steps and begin on a separate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of the technical disclosure must commence on a separate sheet under the heading “Abstract” or “Abstract of the Disclosure.” The abstract may not exceed 150 words and its purpose is to enable quick determination of the nature and gist of the technical disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should be a concise narrative limited generally to 50–150 words and not exceed 15 lines of text; should not include other parts of the application; avoid patent claim legal phrasing (e.g., “means,” “said”); should not state purported merits or speculative applications or compare with the prior art. Content should include what is new in the art; for machines give organization and operation, for articles give method of making, for chemicals give identity and use, for mixtures list ingredients, for processes list steps. For compounds/processes, include process for making and/or a use if not obvious. If modifications/alternatives exist, mention preferred modification/alternative by example. The abstract is prepared by the applicant; OPAP will review and examiner will require or edit as necessary; examiner should check abstract compliance early in prosecution and may require revisions via office action or formal amendment on allowance (see MPEP § 1302.04). Sample abstracts are provided for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract drafting tone and length constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be in narrative form, generally limited to a single paragraph within the range of 50 to 150 words, and should not exceed 15 lines of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract helps readers decide whether to consult the full patent text, avoid repeating title information or using phrases that can be implied (e.g., “This disclosure concerns”), and keep language clear and concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for and review of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the abstract is the responsibility of the applicant; the examiner reviews the abstract for compliance and may edit or require correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will review applications for compliance and require an abstract if missing. If abstract does not comply, examiner should point out the defect in the first Office action or at earliest point; replies should be treated under 37 CFR 1.111(b) practice. On allowance, examiner may make necessary revisions by formal examiner’s amendment after obtaining applicant authorization rather than issuing a Quayle action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing submission and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A “Sequence Listing” requirement applies to all nucleotide/amino acid sequences disclosed in an application, whether claimed or not, and must comply with 37 CFR 1.821–1.825.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sequence listing is on paper, follow the relevant CFR and MPEP §§ 2421–2431; if on compact disc, include reference and number of discs/files. See MPEP § 2421.02 for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling applications lacking an abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application does not contain an abstract as required by 37 CFR 1.72(b), the Office will require an abstract on a separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: for pro se applicants, consider using form paragraphs 6.14 to 6.16. Do not use this form paragraph during national stage prosecution of international applications if an abstract was published under PCT Article 21.
